 ‘It’s a shame’: Patrice Neveu frustrated with Togo’s AFCON defeat to Algeria 
 ‘It’s a shame’: Patrice Neveu frustrated with Togo’s AFCON defeat to Algeria
 Dennis Mabuka Togo national team coach Patrice Neveu FTF-Fédération Togolaise de Football﻿ Togo national team coach Patrice Neveu was left frustrated with the outcome of their matchday three fixture of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifiers against Algeria at Hocine Ait Ahmed Stadium, Tizi Ouzou City, Algeria, on Saturday.
 In a Group I fixture which the Sparrowhawks dominated, the final result was not pleasing for the Frenchman, who watched as his side suffered a 1-0 defeat.
 The Togolese defence, anchored by Djene Dakonam and Lilian Brassier, managed to contain the Fennecs repeated attacks throughout the first half and much of the second, repelling offensive thrusts led by Amine Gouiri and Mohamed Amoura.
 However, spurred on by a passionate crowd, the Algerians finally found a way through just as the final quarter of an hour began. 
 In the 76th minute, captain Ramy Bensebaini managed to break through the Togolese defence to score the game’s only goal, after being set up perfectly by Anis Hadj Moussa .
 ‘It’s very regrettable’
 “We had prepared well for this match. The players worked hard on the system we had put in place. Then, on one ball, we weren’t there and, unfortunately, we conceded that goal,” Neveu told reporters after the game.
 “It’s a very frustrating defeat for my players and for the team. My players truly gave a great image of Togolese football. Unfortunately, we didn’t get any points here. It’s very regrettable.”
 Neveu, however, acknowledged the quality of Algeria saying they played to their strengths, and were boosted with the presence of their technically gifted attackers. 
 “Algeria played to their strengths, with technically gifted attacking players. They are a very technical team, with good defenders as well. We knew we were facing a high-quality team,” added Neveu.
 “We really managed to control the game well. It’s a shame, once again, that ball where we weren’t in the right place, but that’s the story of the match.” 
 Togo will not give up
 With the two teams set to face off again in three days’ time, Neveu said: “Time for recovery. The players will unwind a bit, and then we’ll have to get everyone back on track.
 “We know that Algeria has very impressive squad depth. Now, we’re not going to give up until the very end. We’re playing at home, in front of our fans.” 
 The defeat left Togo four points behind leaders Algeria, and one behind second-placed Zambia . Togo had won their opener 1-0 against Burundi before losing 2-0 against the Chipolopolo.
 Asked about Togo’s chances to qualify from the group, Neveu said: "I think we absolutely have what it takes to get back into the race, provided we get a result at home in the return match.” 
 Togo lost against Algeria on Saturday. FTF-Fédération Togolaise de Football . On playing at Hocine Ait Ahmed Stadium, he said: “The atmosphere of the match was extremely pleasant for everyone.
 “Playing in this magnificent stadium, with a great atmosphere... It's the image we would like to see at every match. A wonderful crowd, which provides good conditions for expression. 
 “You saw it on the field: my players are highly motivated, in line with the dynamic I’m trying to instil in them.”
 On whether he will make changes to his squad for the return match against Algeria, Neveu responded: “Yes, there will be changes. I already have one player injured, a regular starter. Besides that, I know my squad depth well; I know my players very well. 
 “We will definitely need to bring in some fresh legs, while also taking stock of the players who performed well in today's match, and of the experienced players, who will know how to recover and come back for the return match.”
 Neveu concluded: “For now, there’s nothing negative. We have one more match at home, to give it our all and push as hard as we can to get some points.” 
 Togo will now host Algeria at the Kegue Stadium on Tuesday.
